ev.q: CDC analyzed data from the Census of Fatal Occupational Injuries (CFOI) for 2003--2008
Occupational highway transportation fatality rates declined 2.8% annually during 2003--2008
representing 24% of all fatal occupational injuries for the period
The annual average fatality rate for workers was 0.9 highway transportation deaths per 100,000 workers
That rate was significantly greater than the rates seen for any other racial or ethnic group
the cross-sectional nature of this analysis allows for identification of associations between exposure and incidents
The fatality rate decreased an estimated 2.8% annually during the period (p=0.0268).
Fatality rates were calculated as highway transportation deaths occurring within a state

methods_quotes.q: Trends and demographic differences were assessed using Poisson regression and significance set at α = 0.05.
To calculate fatality rates, labor force denominator estimates were derived from the Current Population Survey (CPS) for U.S. workers aged ≥16 years
Fatality rates were calculated as highway transportation deaths occurring within a state, using employment data within the state from CPS for the 6-year period.
